findings.summary: No green regression exercises acquisition timeout and proves the new owner cleanup path reaches a terminal, token-free state.
findings.diagnosis: Both real-owner tests use install_owner_gate(), whose patched transaction method calls acquired.set() immediately, so their new wait_for calls always take the success path and their finalizers see an owner already completed by guard_completion. The retained RED only shows that the pre-fix version hangs until an external shell timeout; it cannot assert that the repaired acquisition-timeout path cancels and reaps the owner or clears transaction ownership. Reverting either wait_for to an unbounded wait, or removing the new cancellation/reap lines, leaves every retained green test unchanged.
findings.evidence: install_owner_gate() sets acquired at line 79. The new bounded waits are at lines 283 and 323, while cleanup is at lines 293-296 and 344-347. owner-acquisition-counterfactual-red.log contains only the pre-repair shell exit 124, and the changed/focused green logs exercise the normal acknowledged gate.
findings.correction: Add a controlled no-acknowledgement seam and a green test that expects the bounded acquisition timeout, then asserts the owner is terminal and RuntimeManager._transaction_owner is None. The same counterfactual should fail or hang against the pre-fix structure while completing cleanly after the repair.
